title: Expected Number of Shared Birthday Pairs

problemStatement.plain: In a group of n people with 365 equally likely birthdays, the expected number of pairs sharing a birthday is C(n,2)/365. With 28 people, we expect more than 1 shared pair.
whyMatters: Natural extension of the birthday problem (Wiedijk #93) to expected pairs
Demonstrates linearity of expectation in a classic setting
The 28-person threshold for E[pairs] > 1 contrasts with the 23-person threshold for P(match) > 1/2

# Birthday Problem OQ-01: Expected Shared Pairs

## Status: COMPLETE
8 theorems, 1 definition, 0 sorries. Added to existing BirthdayProblem.lean.

## Key Results
- expected_shared_pairs(n) = C(n,2)/365
- E[23] = 253/365 ~ 0.693
- E[28] > 1 (first n with expected pairs > 1)
- E[27] < 1 (threshold is sharp)

## Proof Technique
Direct computation using Nat.choose and norm_num for concrete values.
